paper_metadata.title: Cracking mechanisms in additively manufactured pure tungsten from printing single tracks, thin walls and cubes

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Cracking is a critical issue in the additive manufacturing of pure tungsten (W).

evidence.section: 4.1. Nanopore weakening effect in PBF – LB W

evidence.quote: The body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal structure of pure W challenges the initiation of motion within its slip systems due to the limited mobility of dislocations, thereby restricting the number of active independent slip systems [6].
IPF maps reveal two regions regardless of the FZ sizes: the columnar grains perpendicular to the FZ boundary and the equiaxed grains in the FZ center.
The investigation reveals that irrespective of the FZ size, the equiaxed grain sizes range from 5 to 6.5 μ m, exhibiting similar grain dimensions across varying scanning speeds.
The microstructure in a unidirectional manner exhibits a ladder-like arrangement, where rectangular grains adjacent to each other are confined between two neighboring scan vectors.
The bidirectional microstructure exhibits a curved, epitaxial columnar grain structure with an extremely large aspect ratio, spanning hundreds of microns.

evidence.section: Abstract

evidence.section: 5. Conclusions
